article.articleHeadline: Hepatitis E Clusters in Shanghai Map to Dense Urban Neighborhoods Near
article.articleSummary: HEV infections in Shanghai were analyzed across 4,668 confirmed cases from 2017–2022, drawn from China’s National Notifiable Disease Reporting System, for an average annual rate of 3.14 per 100,000. HEV transmission is mainly fecal-oral via contaminated water, with zoonotic risk from undercooked pork, seafood, and other animal products. A six-year temporal-spatial analysis identified a significant time cluster Jan 1, 2017–May 31, 2019 (RR 1.35; LLR 52.18) and a winter-to-spring seasonal peak (December–May). Spatially, one primary cluster (RR 1.73; LLR 135.74) emerged, centered in central urban districts with secondary clusters in peri-urban suburbs; raw case counts were highest in dense areas, but the cluster remained strongest when adjusted for population. Logistic regression linked higher density (OR 7.367), more shopping malls (OR 1.531), and shorter distance to rivers (OR 0.742) with clustering. Mechanisms remain unresolved.

article.articleHeadline: India Highlights UHC, Hepatitis, Sickle Cell Care at UNGA81
article.articleSummary: At UNGA81 side events in New York (September 25), India outlined progress on universal health coverage, hepatitis elimination, and sickle cell care. Union Health Secretary Salila Srivastava highlighted the Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (over 180,000 facilities) and AB-PMJAY financial protection, plus Free Drugs and Diagnostics Service and the National Dialysis Programme to reduce out‑of‑pocket costs. A growing digital health ecosystem was noted, with over 900 million citizens having unique health IDs and 497 million e-Sanjeevani teleconsultations, supported by interoperable registries and ABHA-enabled records. On hepatitis, India targets elimination of Hepatitis B and C by 2030; screening has reached nearly 225 million since 2018 across NHM facilities, with 1,039 treatment centres. Integrated prevention, including mother‑to‑child transmission, is emphasized. For sickle cell care, India co‑hosted OneSCD with partners such as Nigeria, WHO, UNICEF, Africa CDC, World Coalition on SCD, and St. Jude, to advance equitable care.

article.articleHeadline: Вирусолог предупредила о новом варианте гонконгского гриппа
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A virologist warned about a new variant of the Hong Kong flu.
article.articleSummary: A fundamentally new variant of Hong Kong influenza (influenza A H3N2) appeared this year. While no pandemic is expected, the variant mutates to evade immune protection and may present distinct symptoms. WHO and influenza surveillance centers have advised updating the current season’s influenza vaccine composition. In Russia, Rosptобnadzor reported detections of swine flu and Hong Kong flu, along with rhinoviruses and parainfluenza. A virologist noted that carriers of the new virus were identified in China on 11 September, with the H3N2 variant not yet replacing circulating strains. Moscow-based infectious disease expert Elena Malinnikova emphasized the new variant’s emergence but reassured that a pandemic is unlikely. The vaccine reform is highlighted as a key seasonal public health measure, while earlier Rosptobnadzor head Anna Popova stated the season features a complete change in vaccine composition.

article.articleHeadline: Ébola en el Congo: prueban vacuna Ervebo en 20.000 trabajadores de primera línea - HSB NOTICIAS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Congo: Ervebo vaccine tested on 20,000 frontline workers - HSB News
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo prompts a BRAVO vaccine trial of Ervebo in frontline workers. The study began on 19 September 2026 in Bunia, Ituri Province, and will follow about 20,000 first responders in Ituri and North Kivu for 9–12 months to assess Ervebo, licensed for Zaire ebolavirus, for protection against Bundibugyo virus—the current outbreak’s cause. WHO notes Ervebo is not licensed for Bundibugyo in humans; its use here proceeds within a research protocol to generate efficacy and safety data and inform future use. The trial is led by MSF and Epicentre, in collaboration with the DRC Ministry of Health, Africa CDC, INRB, and other partners. The international community released 70,000 doses: 20,000 for the phase 3 trial and 50,000 for frontline protection, with informed consent required. The response aims to safeguard healthcare capacity amid a large, ongoing major emergency.

article.articleHeadline: New Antibody Tests Outperform PCR in Detecting Devastating Rice Panicle
article.articleSummary: Dot-ELISA and CGICS, developed by Zhejiang University researchers, detect Burkholderia glumae and B. plantarii, the primary agents of rice bacterial panicle blight (RBPB). The serological tests outperform conventional PCR in sensitivity and require no expensive lab equipment, enabling field and port screening. Antibody pairs: 4A7/8C5 target B. glumae; 12B5/14B3 target B. plantarii; both show high specificity with no cross-reaction to non-target Burkholderia or other rice pathogens. Detection limits: 1.96×10^4 CFU/mL for either pathogen, roughly 2–4× more sensitive than PCR (3.91×10^4 and 7.81×10^4 CFU/mL). In infected grain homogenates, positives at 1:7680 dilution, twice PCR sensitivity (1:3840). RBPB, described in Japan in the 1950s, is now widespread in Africa, Asia, North and South America; Vietnam 1992 outbreak yielded up to 75% yield losses, while typical losses are around 15%.

article.articleHeadline: Três Passos participa de Encontro Estadual de Arboviroses em Porto Alegre - Três Passos News
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Três Passos participates in State Meeting on Arboviral Diseases in Porto Alegre - Três Passos News
article.articleSummary: During September 23–24, 2026, Raquel Rejane de Oliveira, a nurse with the Três Passos Epidemiological Surveillance team, participated in the State Meeting on Arboviral Diseases: Epidemiology, Diagnosis and Clinical Management, held in Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul. The event, hosted at Cremers, gathered public-health professionals to discuss prevention, diagnosis, and response strategies for arboviral diseases—namely dengue, chikungunya, and Zika virus—in the state. For the 2nd Regional Health Coordination, which covers 26 municipalities, seven slots were available. The program addressed clinical management, prevention and control, and epidemiological analysis, fostering exchange of experiences and the joint planning of response strategies.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Virologist: a new variant of Hong Kong flu appeared in 2026 - News on Vesti.ru
article.articleSummary: Moscow, Russia – a fundamentally new variant of the Hong Kong flu (influenza A, subtype H3N2) emerged in 2026, but a pandemic is not expected. Virologist Elena Malinnikova, Doctor of Medical Sciences and infectious disease physician, told RIA Novosti. The World Health Organization has recommended updating the current seasonal influenza vaccine to address this variant. The Hong Kong flu is caused by influenza A (H3N2); its hallmark is rapid onset, with patients potentially going from feeling fine in the morning to high fever and severe symptoms by evening. There has been no replacement of the circulating strain yet; the new variant has appeared without yet triggering a shift.

article.articleHeadline: SSM: three local schools report flu-like illness clusters
article.articleSummary: Influenza-like illness clusters were reported in Macau on Sept. 23, affecting 22 students across three schools, with 12 laboratory-confirmed cases of influenza A. The clusters involve Escola Tong Sin Tong Kindergarten (classes 2B and 3B), Yuet Wah College Chinese Section (class F2E), and Pui Ching Secondary School Coloane Campus (class K3H). Onset of fever and cough began Sept. 18. All cases are mild with no serious complications reported. In response, schools have increased disinfection, cleaning, ventilation and are enforcing isolation protocols for affected students. No travel exposure or other sources are detailed in the report. The Health Bureau notes ongoing surveillance for influenza-like illness and emphasizes routine infection-control measures in school settings.

article.articleHeadline: Ações de combate à malária reforça a importância do diagnóstico precoce e da prevenção
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Malaria control actions reinforce the importance of early diagnosis and prevention.
article.articleSummary: Porto Velho, Brazil, recorded 3,061 malaria cases from January 1 to September 15, 2026, up 8.8% from the same period in 2025. Plasmodium falciparum infections reached 213, with 31 mixed P. vivax + P. falciparum cases. Transmission centers in rural and riverine areas, with the highest case counts in Bacia Leiteira (157), Terra Santa (123), KM 13 / Santa Helena (96), Bairro Novo / BR-364 (91), and Uberaba (71). Authorities intensified active surveillance, field visits, indoor spraying, and distribution of impregnated nets. Free diagnosis and treatment are available via SUS, prioritizing children, pregnant women, the elderly, and rural/ribeirinha populations. Suspect malaria symptoms—fever, chills, headaches, body aches, fatigue—should seek rapid testing or thick-blood smear at local health units promptly.

article.articleHeadline: 7.582 Kasus TBC Ditemukan di Garut, 81 Orang Meninggal Dunia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 7,582 TB cases detected in Garut, 81 people died.
article.articleSummary: 7,582 tuberculosis cases detected in Garut, West Java, as of September 15, 2026, with 81 deaths and 51 drug-resistant cases. TB presence spans Garut from north to south, affecting all age groups. Symptoms include a cough lasting more than two weeks, shortness of breath, chest pain, night sweats, and coughing blood. Prevalence remains above 200 per 100,000 population; national target by 2030 is about 65 per 100,000. Garut Health Office is intensifying active case finding in partnership with the Health Ministry and health partners, integrating screening with the free health check program (CKG) across villages, schools, and posyandu, aided by mobile chest X-ray. Suspected cases are confirmed with rapid molecular testing (TCM). The high case-finding rate reflects expanded screening, not necessarily new transmission, and aims to enable early treatment to reduce deaths and transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Cegah Penularan Rabies, Pemilik Hewan Diimbau Rutin Vaksinasi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Prevent Rabies Transmission: Pet Owners Urged to Vaccinate Routinely.
article.articleSummary: Indonesia's rabies vaccination program for pets—covering dogs, cats, and monkeys—continues in Jakarta to raise animal immunization coverage and curb rabies spread to humans. Pet owners are urged to bring animals for vaccination per the schedule outlined by health officials. Increasing vaccination coverage is seen as essential to build herd immunity in animal populations and reduce the risk of human exposure. Rabies transmits from animals to people chiefly via bites or exposure to infected saliva; vaccination of animals is a key preventive measure. People with dogs or cats and other potential rabies sources should ensure routine vaccination and seek prompt medical care if bitten or exposed. The program aims to raise public awareness and strengthen protection against a disease that can be fatal.

article.articleHeadline: Influenza aviaria, il vaccino a mRNA "auto-amplificante" passa il primo test sull'uomo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Avian influenza, the self-amplifying mRNA vaccine passes the first test in humans.
article.articleSummary: A self-amplifying mRNA vaccine against avian influenza H5N1 (ARCT-2304) produced positive first-in-human data in 212 healthy adults. In a randomized, observer-blind Phase I trial, participants received two doses (1.5, 5, or 12 micrograms) at four- or eight-week intervals, with controls. The vaccine elicited antibodies against both hemagglutinin and neuraminidase and a Th1-skewed T-cell response. Extending the dosing interval to eight weeks yielded higher, more durable antibody responses than four weeks. Neutralizing and neuraminidase-directed antibodies remained above baseline six–seven months after the second dose. Adverse events were mostly transient, mild-to-moderate, and dose-related. Limitations include the small sample size (212) and lack of data on actual protection; the antigen derives from A/Indonesia/5/2005, and further work across variants is needed. Funding from BARDA; most authors affiliated with Arcturus Therapeutics. Not a ready vaccine; promising platform for pandemic preparedness. Publication: Nature Communications, Sept 24, 2026.

article.articleHeadline: NCDC strengthens Ebola surveillance as DRC outbreak sparks fresh alert
article.articleSummary: Nigeria’s NCDC has strengthened Ebola surveillance amid the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) outbreak, instituting enhanced measures for travellers from countries with active or relevant EVD transmission. Travellers may be required to complete Health Declaration Forms to support early detection, risk assessment, contact tracing and rapid response; those from other countries are exempt. Coordination among the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Port Health Services, FAAN, Nigeria Immigration Service and NCAA, with WHO and Africa CDC providing technical support, underpins the new approach. As of September 20, 2026, the DRC outbreak has 7,672 confirmed cases and 3,699 deaths (data through September 19, 2026); 886 patients are in isolation, and 1,879 Bundibugyo virus variant infections have recovered. Affected provinces include Ituri, North Kivu, Haut-Uélé and Tshopo. Symptoms to monitor: fever, weakness, muscle pain, headache, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, bleeding.

triage.notes: 記事はDRCで進行中のエボラ流行（Bundibugyoウイルス変異株）とそれに対するナイジェリアの水際対策強化を報じている。ナイジェリアは発生国ではなく対策強化国であるため、verified_locationsにはDRCのみを記載。

article.articleHeadline: Batuk dan Demam Tak Membaik 3 Hari? Waspadai Influenza A dan Risiko Pneumonia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cough and fever not improving for 3 days? Watch out for Influenza A and the risk of pneumonia.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A infection should not be treated as a common cold; it can weaken the immune system and raise the risk of pneumonia by allowing bacteria to reach the lungs. In Jakarta, Dr. Joyce Bratanata explains that the influenza virus undermines host defenses, creating a gateway for bacterial infections. Early influenza symptoms resemble other ARIs and include high fever, sore throat, and dry cough. If cough and fever persist for three days, seek medical care promptly, rather than waiting for breathlessness. Early testing with influenza antigen swab or PCR panel identifies the cause and guides therapy, reducing inappropriate antibiotic use. Antivirals are not needed for all patients; they’re given to those with clear indications or high risk (young children starting school, the elderly, and those with comorbidities). Public health updates indicate spread across 38 provinces, with East Java among the highest.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 100 HIV Cases Detected in West Sulawesi from January–August 2026, Majority of Patients Are Men Who Have Sex With Men
article.articleSummary: As of Sept 24, 2026, West Sulawesi Province, Indonesia, identified 100 new HIV cases (PLHIV) for January–August 2026, with 91 on antiretroviral therapy (ART). District distribution: Polman 41 cases (40 on ART), Mamuju 30 (26 on ART), Majene 14 (11 on ART), Mamuju Tengah 7 (all on ART), Pasangkayu 7 (6 on ART), Mamasa 1 (on ART). MSM (men who have sex with men) represent 41% of cases, followed by TB coinfection at 20%. The data indicate broad ART access across districts as a key strategy to preserve immune function and reduce transmission. Case identification occurred largely through formal healthcare facilities. This update reflects provincial health reporting up to 24 September 2026.

triage.notes: 地方保健当局によるルーティンのHIVサーベイランス報告であり、ART普及率など対策が機能していることを示す内容。

article.articleHeadline: エボラ熱感染疑いの死者埋葬巡り混乱、1人死亡　コンゴ東部、治安部隊発砲
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Chaos over the burial of a person suspected of Ebola infection; one dead. Eastern Congo, security forces opened fire.
article.articleSummary: Security forces opened fire during the burial of a person suspected of Ebola infection in North Kivu, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, on September 24, killing one. Local residents, eager to view the body, clashed amid traditions that involve touching and mourning the deceased, prompting specialist teams to conduct burials to reduce transmission. Attacks on treatment facilities followed as distrust of health workers grows, fueled by misinformation that Ebola is a Western conspiracy. The Democratic Republic of the Congo’s health ministry reports 7,820 Ebola infections and 3,779 deaths to date. The outbreak involves the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain, which has no approved vaccine, and officials say there is no clear end in sight. Reuters reported these events.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ熱感染疑いの死者埋葬巡り混乱、1人死亡　コンゴ東部、治安部隊発砲
triage.triage_reason: DRC東部で感染者7,820人・死者3,779人に達する大規模エボラアウトブレイクが継続中で、ワクチン未承認株による管理困難、治安悪化・医療従事者への攻撃も発生しており、公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的関心が高い。
triage.notes: 既に7,820人感染・3,779人死亡という大規模アウトブレイク。ワクチン未承認のBundibugyo株であり、住民の不信感・治安部隊の発砲など社会的混乱も拡大している。続報として国際的拡大の有無を注視する必要あり。

article.articleHeadline: Waspada Influenza Tipe A Pemicu Pneumonia dan Kelompok Rentan
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Be vigilant: Influenza Type A, a trigger for pneumonia and vulnerable groups.
article.articleSummary: Influenza Type A can significantly weaken the immune system and trigger pneumonia. In Indonesia, Dr. Joyce Bratanata, Sp.PD, speaking at a Pfizer Indonesia health event in Jakarta, urges vigilance if cough and runny nose persist for three days with fever. Early influenza A symptoms resemble other acute respiratory infections (ARIs); prompt medical evaluation with influenza antigen swab or PCR panel is advised to confirm etiology and guide therapy. Antiviral treatment is not universally required and is prioritized for patients with clear clinical indications or those in high‑risk groups vulnerable to deterioration. Transmission is airborne, so prevention emphasizes proper mask use, hand hygiene, and avoiding smoking indoors, alongside annual influenza vaccination, which covers both influenza A and B strains. Vaccination is a key measure to reduce transmission and severity. (Jakarta, Indonesia; 25 September 2026).

triage.headline_ja: 警戒:肺炎や脆弱層のリスクを高めるA型インフルエンザ
triage.triage_reason: 医師による一般的な健康啓発・予防啓発記事であり、具体的な集団発生やアウトブレイクの報告ではない。
triage.notes: 記事は季節性インフルエンザに関する一般的な啓発・予防情報であり、特定のアウトブレイクや症例急増を報告するものではない。

article.articleHeadline: 2.18L bite cases, 14 rabies deaths: Stray dogs continue to hound Kerala
article.articleSummary: Kerala reports 2.18 lakh dog-bite cases and 14 rabies deaths so far this year, with Kollam recording four rabies fatalities and Thiruvananthapuram three—the highest among districts. Despite a Supreme Court order to remove stray dogs from public places, progress on shelters and related infrastructure remains slow as local bodies struggle to establish facilities. Persistent gaps in sterilisation, vaccination, and shelter capacity hinder control efforts. Although the state has a euthanasia protocol, its rollout is stalled by demands for dedicated facilities, trained personnel, and transport, according to a LSGD official; an ABC centre or kennelled site is required, along with vehicles and dog catchers. Former chief secretary A. Jayathilak had directed district collectors to identify forest land along boundaries for shelters, but no district has submitted suitable land, despite a ministerial reminder.

triage.headline_ja: 犬咬傷21.8万件、狂犬病死14人：ケララ州で野良犬問題が続く
triage.triage_reason: インドのケララ州で狂犬病による死亡が継続的に報告されているが、狂犬病は同地域で地方風土病として既知であり、異常な発生や国際的拡大の兆候はない。ただし制御体制（不妊化・ワクチン接種・シェルター整備）の遅れが続いており、状況の推移を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 狂犬病はインドで地方風土病であり、今回の報告は既存の公衆衛生課題（野良犬管理、ワクチン接種率の低さ）を反映したもの。新規または異常な感染拡大の兆候はなく、フルリスク評価よりも継続的な経過観察が適切と判断。

article.articleHeadline: 17,939 dengue cases, nine deaths in TN so far in 2026
article.articleSummary: Dengue cases in Tamil Nadu reached 17,939 with nine deaths through Sept 23, 2026. Districts Chennai, Coimbatore, Salem, Thiruvallur, and Chengalpet recorded the most fever cases. A total of 2,23,000 tests were conducted in the first nine months, with fever monitoring in 5,818 facilities. Health Secretary Dr Darez Ahamed stated 26,303 health workers are deployed and Rapid Response Teams are conducting field monitoring. Following a Chennai student’s death from scrub typhus, authorities have initiated mass cleaning in all schools and government colleges. He denied reports of medicine scarcity in Sick Newborn Care Units, noting stocks are available. The year’s dengue activity is lower than 2025 (25,585) and 2024 (35,000). No details on infection sources or laboratory confirmation are provided beyond testing counts.

triage.headline_ja: タミル・ナードゥ州、2026年これまでにデング熱17,939例・死亡9名
triage.triage_reason: デング熱は例年発生する既知の風土病で今年は前年より少なく、IHR基準には該当しないが、行政が積極的に対応しており継続的なモニタリング対象とする。
triage.notes: デング熱は例年発生しており前年比で件数減少。ツツガムシ病による学生死亡を受けた学校の清掃活動が言及されているが、詳細な感染源や検査確定情報は不足。

article.articleHeadline: Kasus Influenza Meningkat, Kemenkes Sebut Risiko Penularan Rendah
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Influenza cases on the rise, Health Ministry says transmission risk is low.
article.articleSummary: Indonesia's Health Ministry spokesperson Widyawati says global influenza activity is rising, but domestic transmission remains low. Data through week 36 of 2026 show influenza activity in Indonesia remains low and under control. The dominant subtype detected is Influenza A (H1N1pdm09). Surveillance continues to monitor case trends and viral characteristics, including severity, though no specific case counts are provided. Authorities urge calm and to follow official government updates on influenza. Preventive measures include handwashing with soap and water, cough and sneeze etiquette, environmental hygiene, adequate rest, and nutritious meals. People with influenza-like symptoms should wear masks when outside and reduce close contact to prevent spread. Although influenza is generally mild and self-limiting, seek medical care if symptoms worsen or do not improve.

triage.headline_ja: インフルエンザ患者数増加、保健省は感染リスクは低いと発表
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザ(H1N1pdm09)の活動は保健省自身が「低リスクで管理下にある」と明言しており、異常性・重症性・拡大リスクのいずれも認められない。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザの定期サーベイランス報告であり、具体的な症例数やクラスター発生の記述はない。当局は国民に冷静な対応と基本的な予防策の遵守を呼びかけている。

article.articleHeadline: 曾去富國島！彰化夫妻返台「發燒、肌肉痛」染登革熱 同團21人健康追蹤
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Visited Phu Quoc Island! Couple from Changhua back in Taiwan with fever and muscle pains, diagnosed with dengue fever; 21 people in the same tour group under health surveillance.
article.articleSummary: Two imported dengue fever cases in Changhua County, Taiwan, involve a middle-aged couple who toured Phu Quoc Island, Vietnam, from Sep 12–15 and developed fever, headache, and rash on Sep 19–20. Lab confirmation (NS1 positive) on Sep 23 and sequencing by the CDC confirmed infection as overseas-imported from Vietnam; both patients are hospitalized. No local transmission is suspected since there have been no prior cases nearby and residence, with a time/distance gap. A tour group of 21 other travelers across Taichung, Tainan, Hsinchu, and Nantou is under health surveillance. Public health actions include a survey of 75 surrounding households, finding 38 standing water containers, 13 of which tested positive for vector density; chemical control was implemented on Sep 24. Authorities urge travellers to dengue-endemic areas to prevent bites and seek care within two weeks of return if symptomatic, informing travel history.

triage.headline_ja: 富国島に行っていた！彰化の夫婦が台湾帰国後「発熱、筋肉痛」でデング熱感染 同じツアー団21人を健康観察
triage.triage_reason: 台湾在住者のベトナム渡航による輸入症例2例で、現地二次感染の兆候はなく、対象国（ベトナム）における国内発生イベントとしての重大性は認められない。
triage.notes: 感染は台湾在住者がベトナム・富国島旅行中に罹患した輸入症例であり、記事の主題は台湾国内での対応（媒介蚊対策・健康観察）である。ベトナムは対象国リストに含まれるが、記事の主題はベトナムでの発生ではなく台湾での輸入症例対応であるため、verified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Antisipasi "Super Flu", Pemkab Bandung Siagakan 2.601 "Bed" dan 62 Puskesmas
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Anticipating the "Super Flu", Bandung Regency Government Deploys 2,601 Beds and 62 Community Health Centers.
article.articleSummary: Bandung Regency, West Java, Indonesia, is bolstering readiness for a potential 'super flu' surge by deploying 2,601 beds across 62 community health centers (puskesmas) and 18 hospitals, with stocked supportive medications. The Dinas Kesehatan monitors influenza-like illness (ILI), acute respiratory infections (ISPA), and other potential outbreaks under the Early Warning and Response System (SKDR), with no random field testing since facilities are not sentinel for ILI. Emphasis is on preventive measures: handwashing with soap, cough etiquette, and masking, noting influenza as a self-limiting disease and prioritizing individual immunity. In case of high ED (IGD) demand, triage remains and mild cases may be managed outpatient. Two-week data up to late September 2026 show ILI rising 53.3% and ISPA rising 36.38%, aligning with observed respiratory case increases in the region.

triage.headline_ja: 「スーパーフル」に備え、バンドン県政府が2,601床と62のプスケスマスを準備
triage.triage_reason: ILI/ISPAの増加率上昇と地域の医療体制強化の動きはあるが、病原体の異常性・重症度・死亡例等の具体的情報がなく、自己限定性疾患と明記されているためフルRRA移行の根拠は現時点で不足している。
triage.notes: 記事は『スーパーフル』という通俗的表現を使用しているが、内容はインフルエンザ様疾患（ILI）とISPAの増加に対する地域の予防的医療体制強化であり、新型・変異株等の異常性を示す記述はない。続報でウイルス型・重症度データの有無を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Tamil Nadu: Special dengue ward opened at Thoothukudi Government Hospital amid rising cases
article.articleSummary: Thoothukudi Government Medical College Hospital in Tamil Nadu opened dedicated dengue wards as dengue cases rise amid the monsoon season. The adult ward has about 60 beds and the paediatric ward about 40 beds, all isolated and netted to prevent transmission. Diagnostic testing and treatment are in place; the facility stocks IV fluids, plasma, blood components, and essential medicines. Medical Superintendent Dr R Padmanabhan said the wards will admit patients with dengue-like symptoms and ensure close monitoring, noting dengue’s three-phase progression: febrile phase with high fever, followed by a critical phase around day five or six with severe abdominal pain, vomiting, muscle pain, and extreme fatigue. Platelet counts may fall sharply during the critical phase, raising bleeding risk. Officials urged community measures to prevent mosquito breeding—removing stagnant water and keeping water containers covered—and the hospital remains able to scale up capacity if admissions increase during the monsoon.

triage.headline_ja: タミル・ナードゥ州:デング熱患者増加に伴い、トゥーットゥックディ政府病院に専用デング熱病棟を開設
triage.triage_reason: 季節性のデング熱患者増加に対する医療機関の通常対応であり、深刻な異常事象ではないが、モンスーン期の流行拡大リスクがあるため継続監視とする。
triage.notes: モンスーン期のデング熱季節的増加に対する地方病院の対応報告。地域限定的で重症度・死亡者数等の詳細情報は不明。インド国内の毎年恒例の事象である可能性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Geger 'Super Flu' Terdeteksi di 13 Provinsi RI, Terbanyak Ada di Sini
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Frenzy over 'Super Flu' Detected in 13 Indonesian Provinces, Most Cases Found Here
article.articleSummary: Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K, nicknamed 'Super Flu', has been detected in 13 Indonesian provinces since January 2026, with 76 cumulative cases reported as of September 19, 2026 (week 37). The highest counts are in East Java and South Kalimantan (18 each), followed by West Java (12) and DKI Jakarta (11); others include Sumatera Selatan (5), Sumatera Utara (3), Bali (2), Nusa Tenggara Timur (2), Nusa Tenggara Barat (1), Sulawesi Utara (1), Jawa Tengah (1), Sulawesi Selatan (1), and DI Yogyakarta (1). Subclade K is a mutation within seasonal influenza A(H3N2), not a new virus, but potentially more aggressive due to faster replication in the respiratory tract and shorter incubation, with symptoms including high fever (39–41°C), severe myalgia, extreme fatigue, dry cough, headache, and sore throat. High-risk groups are young children, the elderly, and individuals with heart disease, cancer, HIV, or immunosuppression. Surveillance data cited from Indonesia’s Ministry of Health, with IDAI context.

triage.headline_ja: 「スーパーフル」インドネシア13州で検出、大騒ぎに 最多はこの地域
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザA(H3N2)のサブクレードKで新規ウイルスではないが、複数州で拡大し重症化リスクの懸念があるため、続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザA(H3N2)の変異株（サブクレードK）で、新規病原体ではない。重症度・死亡数についての具体的データが記事に不足しており、入院率や死亡者数は不明。インドネシア保健省の通常サーベイランスの一環として報告されている点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: 彰化夫妻赴越南富國島旅遊染登革熱　衛生局籲出國做好防蚊、返國14天留意健康 - 健康新聞 - PChome Online 新聞
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A Changhua Couple Contracted Dengue Fever While Traveling to Phu Quoc Island, Vietnam; Health Bureau Urges Mosquito Precautions While Abroad and Health Monitoring for 14 Days After Returning.
article.articleSummary: Two imported dengue fever cases in Changhua County, Taiwan, linked to travel to Phu Quoc Island, Vietnam. A middle-aged couple traveled September 12–15 on a tour; after returning, they developed headache, fever, and rash on September 19–20. Laboratory testing confirmed dengue as imported. Health authorities report ongoing monitoring of fellow tour members and close contacts. Southeast Asia remains a dengue-endemic region, so travelers are urged to employ strict personal mosquito protection abroad and to practice self-monitoring for at least 14 days after returning. The incident highlights the risk of travel-associated dengue and the need for post-travel surveillance to limit potential local transmission.

triage.headline_ja: 彰化の夫婦がベトナム・フーコック島旅行でデング熱に感染　衛生局が海外での防蚊対策と帰国後14日間の健康観察を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 台湾在住者の輸入症例2例であり、ベトナム国内での異常な流行拡大や重症化を示す情報はなく、東南アジアの風土病としての通常の輸入例に留まる。
triage.notes: 本事例は台湾人渡航者の輸入症例であり、ベトナム国内での発生状況を主題とした記事ではないため、Vietnamは対象国リストに含まれるが本記事の主題国発生ではなく除外。台湾は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations は空配列。

article.articleHeadline: 彰化夫妻富國島旅遊返台確診登革熱住院中 同團21人狀況曝
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Changhua couple on Phu Quoc Island tour diagnosed with dengue fever on returning to Taiwan, hospitalized; conditions of 21 people in the same tour group revealed.
article.articleSummary: Two imported dengue fever cases in Taiwan: a Changhua County couple in their 50s who traveled with relatives to Phu Quoc Island, Vietnam from Sept 12–15 and returned with fever and myalgia on Sept 19–20. They sought outpatient care, then emergency care; NS1 rapid test positive and diagnosed on Sept 23; specimens sent to the CDC for sequencing; both hospitalized. Local transmission ruled out; infection source considered Vietnam-imported. The tour group comprised 21 people across Taichung, Tainan, Hsinchu and Nantou; authorities notified health bureaus for follow-up. Household investigations around the case’s residence found 75 households with 38 standing-water containers, 13 positive; vector density high; chemical control conducted on Sept 24. Public health guidance urges prevention: eliminate standing water, wear light clothing, use approved repellents (DEET, Picaridin, IR-3535), seek medical care for dengue-like symptoms and report travel history; clinics should perform TOCC screening and consider NS1 tests for early detection.

triage.headline_ja: 彰化の夫婦、フーコック島旅行から台湾帰国後にデング熱と診断され入院、同ツアー21人の状況が判明
triage.triage_reason: 台湾における個別の輸入デング熱症例であり、現地伝播は否定され、迅速な媒介対策も実施済み。対象国（ベトナム等）での流行拡大を示す情報はなく、社会的関心の高まりも確認できない。
triage.notes: 台湾での輸入症例報告であり、対象国リストに台湾は含まれない。ベトナムは感染源として言及されているが、記事はベトナム国内の流行状況を報じるものではなく、台湾側の対応・調査結果が主題であるため、Vietnamは含めなかった。

article.articleHeadline: Thoothukudi hospital opens special dengue wards as cases rise
article.articleSummary: Thoothukudi Government Medical College Hospital, Tamil Nadu, opened dedicated adult (60-bed) and paediatric (40-bed) dengue wards amid a seasonal rise in dengue cases during the monsoon. Approximately 100 isolation beds are in place, with mosquito nets, sufficient medicines, IV fluids, plasma, and blood components. Diagnostic testing and treatment infrastructure are available for patients with high fever and dengue-like symptoms. Dengue typically progresses in three phases: febrile phase with high-grade fever, followed by a critical phase with abdominal pain, vomiting, muscle pain, and extreme fatigue, during which platelet counts can plummet (thrombocytopenia) and bleeding risk rises. Community measures to prevent transmission include removing stagnant water and keeping water containers covered. The hospital can scale bed capacity and resources if admissions rise, and prompt medical evaluation for high fever is urged during the monsoon season.

triage.headline_ja: トゥートゥックディ市の病院、デング熱患者増加に伴い専用病棟を開設
triage.triage_reason: モンスーン期の季節性デング熱増加に対する通常の医療対応記事であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。SFTSウイルスへの言及は本文になし。
triage.notes: 疾患名にSFTS Virusが含まれているが、記事本文・サマリーはデング熱の季節的増加と病院の病床拡充に関する内容のみで、SFTSに関する記述は一切ない。インドの毎年恒例の季節性デング対策記事と判断。

article.articleHeadline: Hati-Hati, Komplikasi Influenza A Bisa Berujung pada Pneumonia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Watch Out: Complications of Influenza A Can Lead to Pneumonia.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A can weaken the immune system and, in severe cases, trigger pneumonia, warns Dr. Joyce Bratanata in Jakarta (Sept 25). Early symptoms include sore throat and dry cough; if three days with fever, seek medical care. Diagnosis by swab, rapid antigen test, or PCR panel helps identify the etiology and guide treatment; antivirals are reserved for clear indications or high-risk patients. High-risk groups include toddlers and young children, elderly, and those with cardiovascular disease, diabetes, asthma, COPD, or immunosuppression (cancer treatment, HIV). Prevention emphasizes masks, handwashing, avoiding indoor smoking, and annual vaccination covering influenza A and B. Influenza A(H3N2) Subclade K (“super flu”) outbreaks: 184 cases across 20 provinces, including Jakarta, East Java, and South Kalimantan; in 2026, 22 cases in six provinces led by Jakarta, Central Java, and South Papua. Age distribution: 0–4 years 38%, 5–9 23.4%, 10–17 21.2%, 18–59 15.8%, 60+ 1.6%.

article.articleHeadline: Vaksin Hewan RI Tembus Afrika, Lindungi Unggas dari 3 Penyakit
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Indonesia's animal vaccine reaches Africa, protects poultry against three diseases.
article.articleSummary: Indonesia's domestically produced animal vaccines have reached Africa for the first time, with 10 poultry vaccines exported to Zambia, Congo, Uganda, and Malawi, valued at about $21.3 million. The vaccines cover Newcastle disease (ND), infectious bronchitis (IB), infectious bursal disease (IBD), along with other avian vaccines including for avian influenza (AI). The export marks a government-supported expansion of the national animal-health industry and aims to open new markets for Indonesian vaccines, most of which are produced by Vaksindo. Indonesia has already been able to meet domestic AI and ND vaccine demands, and production capacity can be directed toward export. Officials say export opportunities remain open to additional countries, though vaccines must pass several regulatory steps before entry to each target market. Quote from Agung Suganda, Director General of Livestock and Veterinary Health, Ministry of Agriculture.

triage.headline_ja: インドネシア産動物ワクチン、アフリカへ進出 家禽を3つの疾病から守る
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はインドネシア産動物用ワクチンの輸出に関する産業・貿易ニュースであり、疾病の発生や流行を報じるものではないため、シグナルとしての該当基準はない。
triage.notes: 記事はワクチン輸出という産業ニュースであり、実際の疾病発生を報じていないため、発生地域として記載されているZambia、Congo、Uganda、Malawi、Indonesiaはいずれも実際の感染症発生地ではない。

article.articleHeadline: US pledges $267 million more to fight Ebola in central Africa
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in central Africa, centered in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, was detected in May 2026 and is described as the second most lethal on record after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. On Sept 23, 2026, during UN General Assembly events, the United States pledged an additional $267 million to fight the outbreak, bringing total U.S. commitments to $886 million (including $107 million from HHS). The funds aim to contain the outbreak at its source by building treatment facilities, expanding diagnostics, and providing medical countermeasures for frontline health workers. Congolese Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka called it a major test, noting mobilization of scientific and operational expertise and recent tangible results. The broader drive seeks to reach about $2 billion in pledges to sustain the response and curb transmission.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Is the mosquito coil not working? Bring home these 7 fragrant trees, dengue will stay 100 arm-lengths away!
article.articleSummary: Published on 2026-09-25, this Bangla piece urges seven fragrant plants to deter mosquitoes and help prevent dengue and malaria, reducing reliance on chemical coils. Seven plants are: citronella and lemongrass (lemon-scented oils used in repellents); tulsi (holy basil) and mint; lavender; carnation (the article notes it contains the natural component pyrethrum that aids in repelling mosquitoes); and rosemary. The article notes their strong aromas repel Aedes mosquitoes, making them suitable for placement on balconies or indoors. Nevertheless, it emphasizes that sanitation remains essential: Aedes can breed in even tiny water accumulations. Weekly home inspections are advised; avoid standing water in plant saucers, coconut husks, tires, or containers; cover vases and other water-holding items. Combining these fragrant plants with diligent water management can help keep dengue and malaria at bay while enriching home greenery.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Changhua Couple Contract Dengue Fever After Traveling to Vietnam; 21 People in the Same Tour Group Tracked Across Four Counties/Cities
article.articleSummary: Two spouses in Changhua County contracted dengue fever after a mid‑September tour to Phu Quoc Island, Vietnam. On September 19–20 they developed fever and myalgia; one also had a rash. NS1 rapid test was positive on September 22, and subsequent sequencing confirmed dengue; both are hospitalized. The exposure occurred in Vietnam during September 12–15, with authorities classifying the infection as overseas imported and not locally acquired. A tour group of 21 people spanning Taichung, Tainan, Hsinchu and Nantou is under health surveillance. Local agencies conducted a home area survey of 75 households, found 38 standing-water containers, 13 of which tested positive; vector density is high and chemical control has been carried out. Hospitals have been asked to strengthen TOCC screening and reporting. The public is urged to prevent mosquito bites when traveling to dengue areas and seek medical care within two weeks of return if unwell.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fifth Fever: Two Deaths in Malappuram Within a Week, Do Not Let Your Guard Down, Get Vaccinated Properly
article.articleSummary: Measles (fifth disease) in Malappuram district reports two deaths within a week: a 1.5-year-old and a 10-month-old, with one death on Wednesday and another in Velavanakkad/Velavannoor on the 15th. By Wednesday, 103 cases are laboratory-confirmed and 476 linked individuals are under investigation, signaling ongoing transmission. The Health Department emphasizes vaccination as the key preventive measure; WHO estimates India experiences about 250,000 measles cases annually. Typical symptoms include fever, red rash, cough, diarrhea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, with airborne spread via droplets from coughing or sneezing. Measles-Rubella vaccine prevents disease; first dose at 9 months and second at 16 months, though it can be given up to age five if missed. Government vaccination is free. District data show first-dose uptake at 86% and second-dose completion at 70%, with about 54,941 births (2021–Sept 2026)未 receiving the first dose and 2.7 lakh fully vaccinated, yielding ~78% overall completion, with notable block-level variations. Three deaths occurred within 15 days among symptomatic children; vaccination drives are being intensified to curb spread.

article.articleSummary: Mass campaign against Aedes aegypti in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, specifically the Barreiro region served by Centro de Saúde Milionários, began at 8:30 on Thursday, September 24, 2026, as part of a citywide effort to curb dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. Belo Horizonte reports this is the 195th mutirão in 2026, with 299 tons of waste removed and about 39,000 properties benefited. The operation involves the Municipal Health Secretariat, the Superintendence of Urban Cleaning, and vector-control agents. Officials emphasize that success depends on public participation to eliminate standing water in planters, gutters, bottles, and other containers that can serve as Aedes aegypti breeding sites. The campaign targets preemptive reduction of mosquito breeding ahead of the period of highest transmission risk for mosquito-borne diseases.

article.articleSummary: Dr. Victor Kingombe, a physician at Kisangani's Ebola Treatment Center, died on September 24 from Ebola, the first doctor to die in Tshopo since the outbreak. Kisangani ETC, with 22 beds and MSF support, remains critical as the province reports 42 confirmed cases and 17 deaths on September 22, rising to 43 confirmed cases and 17 deaths by September 24; twelve health workers have been infected since the start of the epidemic. In North Kivu, survivor Kahindo Manzekele Devotte, cured nearly two weeks ago, chose to stay at the ETC in Kitatumba, Butembo to assist patients and staff. North Kivu remains a major epicenter, with 1,402 confirmed cases and 850 deaths as of September 19 across 16 of 34 health zones.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kupang City Health Office and UNICEF Hold TB Findings and Diagnosis Workshop
article.articleSummary: On 25 September 2026, Kupang City Health Office, in collaboration with UNICEF, held a workshop titled 'Protect the Nation’s Generation: Optimizing Detection and Diagnosis of Pediatric TB at Primary Health Facilities in Kupang City.' The event addresses pediatric tuberculosis in Kupang where symptoms are often nonspecific, delaying diagnosis and risking severe illness or death. For the first time, TB responses in Kupang engaged cross-sector partners—health workers, policy-makers from Bappeda Kota Kupang and Bapperida NTT, academics, and PAUD teachers—as frontline actors. Health Chief drg. Retnowati emphasized early detection and treatment, and urged stigma reduction and strengthened immunization. Kupang also earned Third Place in Accessibility and Quality of Health Services from the Ministry of Home Affairs. UNICEF NTT Head Yudhistira Yewangoe outlined three steps: Find (early detection), Connect (integrate services), and Follow-Up (ensure complete treatment), highlighting the pivotal role of PAUD teachers in delivering the approach.

article.articleHeadline: Influenza A, sejak Pandemi 1918 hingga lonjakan kasus 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Influenza A, from the 1918 pandemic to the 2026 surge in cases.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A remains a respiratory virus with historic pandemics (1918) and swine-origin concern (2009). In 2026, Indonesia tracks Influenza A as not a new pandemic but a virus that evolves. Early 2026 surveillance identified Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K; by September 2026, Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 dominated laboratory findings. Influenza A has eight RNA segments and surface HA and NA proteins; antigenic drift prompts vaccine updates, while antigenic shift can create novel strains and pandemics (1957, 1968, 2009). The virus infects via the respiratory tract; symptoms include fever, cough, runny nose, muscle aches, headache, and fatigue; severe disease can lead to pneumonia and respiratory distress, especially in the elderly, children, pregnant women, and those with comorbidities. H5N1 avian influenza remains monitored: globally 993 human cases with 477 deaths since 2003; in Indonesia, 200 cases with 168 deaths through 2025. WHO regards human-to-human transmission as low, underscoring ongoing animal surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: Influenza A Kembali Merebak di 2026, Ini Fakta H1N1, H3N2 hingga H5N1
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Influenza A Resurfaces in 2026; Here Are the Facts About H1N1, H3N2, and H5N1.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A resurfaces in Indonesia in 2026, with the Ministry of Health (Kemenkes) tracking evolving circulation patterns, notably in Jakarta. Early 2026 drew scrutiny to Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K, once dubbed the “superflu.” By September 2026, Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 dominated laboratory findings. Influenza A is an RNA virus with eight genome segments, featuring hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) surface proteins that define subtypes such as H1N1, H3N2, and H5N1. Typical symptoms include fever, cough, runny nose, myalgia, headache, and fatigue; severe outcomes are possible for the elderly, young children, pregnant women, and those with comorbidities, potentially leading to pneumonia or respiratory failure. Antigenic drift drives gradual antigen changes, necessitating periodic vaccine updates. The report emphasizes ongoing surveillance and regional pattern changes in Indonesia, rather than a new pandemic.

article.articleHeadline: Pemkot Yogyakarta Waspada Influenza Tipe A Perkuat Skrining dan Rujukan
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Yogyakarta City Government on Alert for Influenza Type A; Strengthen Screening and Referrals.
article.articleSummary: As of Sep 24, 2026, Yogyakarta City has not confirmed any Influenza A cases; about eight samples remain under investigation. Mayor Hasto Wardoyo instructed the Health Department and all puskesmas to strengthen early screening and referral systems, with a focus on patients whose influenza-like symptoms persist longer than usual. Health facilities are prepared to perform swab testing and laboratory analyses, including PCR, with sample transport protocols aligned to Covid-19 procedures to prevent introduction of new strains. Typical Influenza A symptoms to watch include sudden high fever with chills, muscle and joint pains, sore throat, headache, extreme fatigue, runny nose, and nasal congestion, lasting about three to four days in the acute phase. The circulating strain in Indonesia is suspected to be H1N1. Symptomatic medications are stocked across government facilities (as of H-2).

triage.headline_ja: ジョグジャカルタ市政府、インフルエンザA型を警戒；スクリーニングと紹介体制を強化
triage.triage_reason: 確定症例はまだなく、8検体が調査中の段階であり、行政による予防的な警戒対応にとどまるため、続報を注視する段階と判断する。
triage.notes: 確定症例はまだ確認されておらず、疑い例8件が検査中の段階。行政による予防的な体制強化の発表であり、実際の感染拡大の証拠は現時点でない。続報で確定症例の有無を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Moving target: Congo's North Kivu province becomes new Ebola hotspot
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has shifted to North Kivu, with the Kitatumba treatment centre in Butembo full (29 beds) as cases surge. Two new treatment centres opened, bringing the provincial total to four. A 10-year-old boy died in triage; MSF notes patients unable to find beds amid rising admissions. Congo has confirmed 7,820 cases and 3,779 deaths as of Tuesday. North Kivu now accounts for about one-third of new infections and deaths, signaling geographic redistribution from Ituri, the worst-affected province, though Ituri shows slowing in some areas per WHO. The outbreak traces to the Bundibugyo Ebola virus, spreading for months with first confirmations in Ituri in May; aid cuts, surveillance gaps, lack of approved vaccines or treatments, and armed conflict hinder response. North Kivu's case fatality exceeds 60%, higher than the national 48%, amid mistrust and attacks on responders.

triage.headline_ja: 移動する標的:コンゴ北キブ州が新たなエボラ出血熱のホットスポットに
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱(ブンディブギョ株)がコンゴ民主共和国で大規模流行中(7,820症例、3,779死亡)であり、致死率60%超、ワクチン未承認、武力紛争による対応困難などIHR・WPRO基準の複数に該当するため。
triage.notes: 承認ワクチン・治療法の不足、資金削減、武力紛争、住民の不信感が対応を妨げており、既存のエボラ流行の悪化・拡大局面と位置づけられる。継続的なモニタリングとフルRRAが必要。

article.articleHeadline: 200 Kucing Jalanan di Blok M Ditargetkan Dapat Vaksin Rabies, Ini Alasannya
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 200 Stray Cats in Blok M Targeted to Receive Rabies Vaccine — Here's Why
article.articleSummary: Rabies vaccination effort targets 200 stray cats in Blok M, South Jakarta, as Sudin KPKP Jakarta Selatan conducts health checks and rabies vaccination for World Rabies Day 2026. The campaign covers Blok M sites including Pasaraya Blok M Hub, Taman Literasi, Blok M Square, Melawai Plaza, Taman Sepeda, and areas around a church, Sentralraya, and BNI. About 60 volunteers from Dinas, KPKP, cat-loving communities, and local subdistrict offices participate. Cats receiving vaccines are tagged with barcode collars for identification; Me-O provides food, Kalbe Animal Health supplies medications, and Pet Tag offers the collars. Jakarta has been rabies-free since 2004, but the city remains vigilant due to borders with rabies-affected regions and high animal mobility.

triage.headline_ja: ブロックM地区の野良猫200匹に狂犬病ワクチン接種を実施、その理由とは
triage.triage_reason: 世界狂犬病デーに合わせた予防的なワクチン接種キャンペーンであり、実際の感染事例や公衆衛生上の異常事態は報告されていない。ジャカルタは2004年以降狂犬病フリー地域。
triage.notes: 記事は予防的な動物ワクチン接種キャンペーンの報道であり、ヒトまたは動物における狂犬病の発生・感染事例の報告ではない。ジャカルタは2004年から狂犬病フリーとされている。

article.articleHeadline: Sterilisasi Kucing Jantan Gratis di Kabupaten Semarang, Upaya Kendalikan Populasi dan Cegah Rabies
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Free Neutering of Male Cats in Semarang Regency, an Effort to Control the Population and Prevent Rabies
article.articleSummary: Semarang Regency's Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (Dispertan) conducted free sterilization of 100 male cats to control street cat populations, at two sites: 75 at the department office and 25 at Puskeswan Tegalwaton. Aligned with World Rabies Day, the program also offers free rabies vaccination to promote routine pet vaccination. Yohana Diah H, Head of Animal Health and Veterinary Public Health (Keswan & Kesmavet), explained that sterilizing male cats is emphasized because one tom can sire multiple females, whereas spaying a female limits reproduction to one animal. Although Central Java remains rabies-free, vaccination is continued as a preventive measure for animal and public health. The initiative drew support from Cat Lovers Ungaran, which sent 35 street cats for sterilization, gathered from streets, markets, and waste disposal sites (TPS).

triage.headline_ja: セマラン県で野良猫対策としてオス猫の無料不妊手術を実施、狂犬病予防も呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 中部ジャワは狂犬病フリー地域であり、記事は予防的な不妊手術・ワクチン接種イベントの紹介であって実際の症例発生報告ではないため。
triage.notes: 記事は狂犬病の実際の発生ではなく、World Rabies Dayに合わせた予防啓発活動（不妊手術・ワクチン接種）の内容であり、地域は狂犬病フリーと明記されている。

article.articleHeadline: അപ്രതീക്ഷിത മഴയ്ക്കു പിന്നാലെ വൈറൽ പനിയുമെത്തി; ഇൻഫ്ലുവൻസ ബാധ കൂടുതൽ കുട്ടികളിൽ
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Viral pneumonia follows the unexpected rain; influenza infection is more common among children.
article.articleSummary: Influenza is spreading in Kerala’s Alappuzha district amid unexpected rain and humid conditions, prompting a health department warning. The influenza virus is circulating more in children, with coughs lasting up to two weeks and pneumonia risk for those with respiratory problems. The department urges vigilance and has ordered hospitals to enforce mask-wearing for all staff and patients and to set up cough corners to manage infectious patients and proper mask disposal. Although influenza vaccines exist, they are not available in government hospitals, and there are calls for free vaccination for children, pregnant women, the elderly, and people with serious health issues. An elderly pneumonia preventive medicine is available; for those over 60, a single-dose regimen provides protection for up to five years. The request is to provide vaccines free via the Department of Senior Citizens.

triage.headline_ja: 予期せぬ雨の後にウイルス性熱も出現：子どもたちの間でインフルエンザ感染が拡大
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザの地域的増加であり、重症例の急増や異常な病原性は報告されていないが、公衆衛生当局が警戒を呼びかけているため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザの通常の流行パターンとみられるが、小児における肺炎リスクや医療体制強化の動きがあるため注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Dinkes Situbondo: Penderita flu-like illness bertambah jadi 92 kasus
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Situbondo Health Office: Patients with flu-like illness increase to 92 cases.
article.articleSummary: As of Sept 25, 2026, Situbondo Health Office in East Java reported influenza-like illness (ILI) cases rising to 92 in week 37 (Sept 13–19, 2026), up from 67. The weekly increase of 25 cases is based on data from puskesmas and government hospitals. ILI cases are spread across 10 kecamatan: Sumbermalang, Mlandingan, Banyuglugur, Bungatan, Kendit, Situbondo, Kapongan, Arjasa, Banyuputih, and Besuki (Puskesmas Widoropayung). Health officials stress surveillance and preventive measures, including hygiene, healthy living, and masking for patients, since transmission occurs readily via droplets when speaking or coughing. There is no laboratory confirmation yet of a super flu in Situbondo; no specimens have been collected or proven in the lab. Authorities continue updating the data to monitor the outbreak and reinforce public health messaging.

triage.headline_ja: スンボンド保健局:インフルエンザ様疾患患者が92例に増加
triage.triage_reason: ILI症例が週次で増加(67→92)しているが、実験室確認はなく病原体・重症度も不明のため、続報を注視する段階と判断。
triage.notes: 10郡にわたりILI症例が増加しているが、病原体の検査室確認は未実施。重症度・死亡例の情報なし。今後の検査結果と症例推移を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: 2,4 Juta Lansia Terserang ISPA, Risiko Influenza Jadi Sorotan
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 2.4 Million Elderly Infected with Acute Respiratory Infections, Influenza Risk Under the Spotlight
article.articleSummary: Indonesia’s Ministry of Health reports over 2.4 million elderly infected with acute respiratory infections (ISPA) from January to August 2026, prompting expanded annual influenza vaccination, especially in densely populated provinces to curb complications. Health Director Imran Pambudi warns influenza in seniors is a serious, under-recognized threat due to immune decline and comorbidities such as hypertension, diabetes, and heart disease, significantly raising pneumonia and death risk if untreated. The burden is worsened by functional limits and cognitive decline, making influenza more contagious and potentially fatal than other ISPA. Case patterns rise at the start of the year, dip mid-year, then surge in August; reports note influenza A, including H3N2, in September 2026. Provinces like West Java, Central Java, East Java, Jakarta, and Banten account for tens of thousands of elderly cases monthly, with Aceh recording 2,902 elderly cases in January 2026, including 35 pneumonia. Globally, WHO estimates 290,000–650,000 influenza deaths yearly, mostly among the elderly.

triage.headline_ja: 高齢者240万人が急性呼吸器感染症に罹患、インフルエンザリスクが注目される
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザ（H3N2含む既知株）に関する通常の公衆衛生報告であり、異常なアウトブレイクや国際的拡大リスクを示す情報はない。
triage.notes: インドネシア保健省による季節性インフルエンザワクチン接種推進キャンペーンの一環としての報告記事。高齢者の基礎疾患による重症化リスクへの注意喚起であり、新興感染症シグナルではない。

article.articleHeadline: 彰化夫妻遊富國島染登革熱「住院治療中」　同團21人分布4縣市
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Changhua Couple Vacationing on Phu Quoc Island Contract Dengue Fever and Are Hospitalized; 21 People in the Group Are Spread Across Four Counties and Cities.
article.articleSummary: Two imported dengue fever cases confirmed in Taiwan: a Changhua County couple in their 50s who traveled to Phu Quoc Island, Vietnam (Sept 12–15) with friends; after returning they developed fever, myalgia, and one with a rash. They sought care, NS1 screening positive; diagnosis confirmed Sep 23. Laboratory samples were sent to the CDC for sequencing, and both are hospitalized. Epidemiologic tracing showed the couple had been in local eateries and shops before onset; their cluster includes 21 other people scattered across Taichung, Tainan, Hsinchu, and Nantou, now under health department surveillance. Local authorities completed 75 household checks, recovering 38 water containers, 13 positive for vectors; chemical control performed. The infection source is considered overseas-imported with no local transmission detected. Emphasizes bite prevention for travelers and prompt medical care with travel history reporting; calls for standing-water elimination to curb vector breeding.

triage.headline_ja: 彰化夫妻遊富國島染登革熱「住院治療中」　同團21人分布4縣市
triage.triage_reason: 台湾における輸入性デング熱の個別症例であり、現地感染は確認されておらず、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響や国際的拡大リスクは低い。
triage.notes: 台湾（対象国リスト外）における輸入例であり、感染地はベトナム・フーコック島。地域封じ込め対応（水源除去・害虫駆除）が完了しており、現地伝播は確認されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Mass test and treat (MTaT) for malaria prevalence in a moderate transmission setting, a quasi-experimental trial from rural Ghana
article.articleSummary: Malaria prevalence in rural Ghana's Pakro subdistrict, Eastern Region, was reduced using mass test and treat (MTaT) over two years in a quasi-experimental study. In 11 communities (7 MTaT, 4 controls), trained community health volunteers conducted five MTaT rounds; rapid diagnostic tests screened individuals and artemether-lumefantrine treated positives. Among 5,309 participants (4,000 intervention; 1,309 control), MTaT coverage rose from 70.6% in March 2020 to 90.7% in March 2022. After adjustment for baselines, overall malaria prevalence by RDT was 84% lower in intervention vs controls (aPR 0.16, 95% CI 0.13–0.20; p<0.001). In children ≤15 years, prevalence fell by 89% (aPR 0.11, 95% CI 0.08–0.14; p<0.001); in those >15 years, reduction was 74% (aPR 0.26, 95% CI 0.18–0.33; p<0.001). The study suggests MTaT could reduce malaria burden in moderate transmission settings; trial NCT04301531 (registered 03/04/2020).

triage.headline_ja: ガーナ地方部における中等度伝播地域でのマラリア有病率に対する集団検査・治療(MTaT)の準実験的試験
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はマラリア対策介入(MTaT)の学術研究報告であり、新規アウトブレイクや異常事態を示すものではないため、シグナルとしての基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: 本記事は既知の風土病であるマラリアに対する研究介入の効果を評価する学術論文であり、公衆衛生上の緊急事態や異常発生を報告するものではない。Coccidioidomycosis（コクシジオイデス症）への言及はサマリー中に見られず、疾患タグの誤付与の可能性がある。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo: Young doctor dies of Ebola as cases surge beyond epicentre
article.articleSummary: As of 25 September 2026, in Congo's Kisangani, Victor Kingombe, a young internal medicine doctor, died of Ebola at the city's Ebola treatment centre, with colleagues and family attending his funeral as healthcare workers in PPE carried his body. Kisangani, capital of Tshopo province, first reported Ebola in late June; the treatment centre was inaugurated less than two weeks prior. While Ituri remains the outbreak's epicentre with a declining trend, neighboring provinces show sharp increases; North Kivu cases rose 73% over the past three weeks. The spread occurs under insecurity, displacement, a health worker strike, and heavy population movement, with rumours and mistrust hindering response and treatment centres and burial teams repeatedly attacked. The WHO says the epidemic could surpass the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak. In August, Congo began vaccinating healthcare workers in Kisangani with Ervebo (Zaire ebolavirus) vaccine, which offers some protection though this outbreak is Bundibugyo; treatment trials are underway nationwide.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国：エボラ感染拡大が震源地を超えて広がる中、若手医師がエボラで死亡
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目中3項目が該当し、WHOが2014-2016年の西アフリカ流行を上回る可能性を指摘するなど、深刻かつ拡大傾向にあるエボラ流行であるためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: Kisangani（Tshopo州）やIturi、North Kivuなど複数州にまたがる拡大が報告されている。治安不安、住民の不信・襲撃、医療従事者ストライキ等が対応を困難にしており、WHOは過去最大級の流行に発展する恐れを警告している。ワクチン（Ervebo）は本流行株（Bundibugyo）に対し部分的な効果に留まる点も懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Kemarau Panjang, Kasus ISPA dan Diare Akut di Bangkalan Meningkat
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Prolonged Drought, Cases of Acute Respiratory Infections and Acute Diarrhea in Bangkalan Have Increased
article.articleSummary: Bangkalan Regency, East Java, Indonesia, reports rising acute respiratory infections (ISPA) and acute diarrhea amid a prolonged dry season. From week 35 to week 37 in 2026, ISPA cases increased from 647 to 831 patients (up 184), while diarrhea rose from 338 to 402 cases. Health official Dr. Nunuk Kristiani attributes the ISPA rise to lower humidity and more dust during the extended dry spell, and the diarrhea rise to reduced access to clean water. Forty-four villages in Bangkalan face a clean-water crisis, compromising sanitation. Additionally, Influenza-Like Illness (ILI) cases reached 404 and suspected typhoid fever 184. All patients are being treated at primary health centers (puskesmas) and hospitals.»

triage.headline_ja: 長引く乾季、バンカラン県で急性呼吸器感染症（ISPA）と急性下痢症例が増加
triage.triage_reason: 乾季による地域内の呼吸器・下痢疾患増加であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低いが、水不足による衛生状態悪化と流行性の可能性があるため経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 記事は地方保健当局によるルーティン報告で、死亡例や重症例の言及はない。44村の清潔な水不足が衛生状態を悪化させており、今後のISPA・下痢・チフス症例の推移を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: 彰化夫妻遊富國島染登革熱 同團21人跨縣市追蹤
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Changhua couple who visited Phu Quoc Island contracted dengue fever; 21 others in the group are being traced across counties and cities.
article.articleSummary: On Sept 25, 2026, a Changhua couple who toured Phu Quoc Island, Vietnam, contracted dengue fever after returning to Taiwan. They developed fever and myalgia; NS1 rapid test was positive on Sept 22 and dengue confirmed on Sept 23, with samples sent for confirmatory testing and sequencing. They are hospitalized. The couple are part of a 21-person travel group spread across Taichung, Tainan, Hsinchu, and Nantou; health authorities began tracing on Sept 23. The township has no local dengue cases this year, suggesting importation, though nearby areas have imported cases. Around their home, 75 residences were surveyed; 38 water containers were positive and 13 contained larvae; chemical control was completed on Sept 24. As of Sept 24, 2026, imported dengue cases total 163 for the year; 2022–2025 totals were 38, 164, 216, and 177. Returnees should seek care within two weeks and remove standing water to reduce risk.

triage.headline_ja: 彰化の夫婦がベトナム・フーコック島旅行後にデング熱に感染、同行の21人を県境を越えて追跡調査
triage.triage_reason: 個別の輸入デング熱症例であり、例年発生している輸入例（年間163例）の範囲内で、公衆衛生上の異常性や国際的拡大のリスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 台湾での輸入症例対応（媒介蚊対策、接触者追跡）は通常の防疫プロセスであり、感染源地はベトナム・フーコック島だが、台湾自体は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。年間輸入症例数は例年の範囲内（2022-2025年:38-216例、2026年163例）で異常な増加は見られない。

article.articleHeadline: Influenza pada Lansia Jadi Ancaman Fata
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Influenza in the Elderly Becomes a Threat to Fata
article.articleSummary: Influenza in Indonesia’s elderly has become a serious health threat amid a September 2026 surge. The Health Ministry warns that influenza in older adults markedly raises the risk of severe pneumonia due to reduced lung and heart reserves, aggravated by high chronic-disease prevalence (SKI 2023: hypertension 63.5%, obesity 14.1%, diabetes 5.7%, pneumonia 5.6%, ISPA 4.6%). About 13% of seniors are dependent, making influenza harder to recover from. Free Health Check (CKG) 2025 found about 7 million seniors with low physical activity; over one-third have central obesity; one-third have cognitive impairment. ISPA covers multiple pathogens; influenza is caused by influenza A, B, or C with fever, dry cough, and myalgia. Jan–Aug 2026 data show >2.4 million elderly ISPA cases, with West Java, Central Java, East Java, DKI Jakarta, and Banten as monthly centers. Global influenza deaths are 290,000–650,000 annually, mostly among the elderly. Recommendations: expand vaccination, routine screening at Puskesmas Santun Lansia, caregiver education, and cross-sector collaboration for elder-friendly environments.

triage.headline_ja: 高齢者のインフルエンザが致命的な脅威に
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザに関する高齢者向け公衆衛生啓発記事であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない通常の季節性事象。
triage.notes: 保健省による季節性インフルエンザと高齢者の健康リスクに関する一般的な注意喚起記事。新興感染症のアウトブレイクではなく、通常の季節性インフルエンザ対策・啓発内容。

article.articleHeadline: 高端腸病毒71型疫苗越南正式開打 首日破萬人登記
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Vietnam officially launches the high-end Enterovirus 71 vaccine; more than 10,000 people register on the first day.
article.articleSummary: On Sept 25, 2026, High-end Vaccine (6547) announced the nationwide rollout of its Enterovirus 71 (EV71) vaccine in Vietnam via the VNVC network, establishing ~300 vaccination centers to shield children from severe EV71-related hand, foot, and mouth disease. On the first day, registrations in major cities including Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Da Nang, and Can Tho reached tens of thousands, with about 70% of enrollees under age 3. High-end Vaccine is the first and currently only EV71 vaccine developer in Vietnam’s public system. In anticipation, Substipharm Biologics and VNVC held Sept 21–22 scientific seminars in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi, titled EV71 HFMD Prevention Era—From Science to Action, and From Taiwan to Vietnam: Real-world Experience in EV71 Vaccine Implementation. Taiwanese experts Huang Limin and Qiu Nanchang shared clinical experience, vaccine durability, booster recommendations for under-2s, and comparisons with other vaccines to support deployment.

triage.headline_ja: 高性能エンテロウイルス71型ワクチン、ベトナムで正式開始 初日で1万人超が登録
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はEV71ワクチンの接種開始に関する広報的な内容であり、疾病の異常な発生や公衆衛生上の緊急性を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事はEV71ワクチンの接種キャンペーン開始を報じるものであり、感染症の発生・流行状況を示す内容ではないため、シグナルトリアージの対象外と判断した。

article.articleHeadline: 高端腸病毒疫苗今在越南開打 打氣爆棚
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Premium enterovirus vaccine rolls out in Vietnam today, with excitement running high.
article.articleSummary: Vietnam begins rollout of Premium Enterovirus 71 (EV71) vaccine on September 25, 2026. The vaccine, developed by Premium Vaccines (6547), is the first EV71 vaccine in Vietnam’s public immunization system, distributed via VNVC (Vietnam Vaccine Joint Stock Company), which has built about 300 vaccination centers and a cold-chain network. On launch day, tens of thousands of vaccination registrations were recorded across Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Da Nang, Can Tho and other areas, with about 70% of applicants under 3 years old, signaling high parental demand. Two scientific seminars in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi (Sept 21–22) featured Taiwan pediatric infectious disease experts Huang Limin and Qiu Nanchang, sharing Taiwan’s experience: since Aug 2023 introduction, Taiwan used over 600,000 EV71 vaccine doses, with no EV71-linked severe hand–foot–mouth disease cases post-vaccination, and ~20% coverage in under-6s. Vietnam obtained regulatory approval in March 2026; first export occurred in August 2026.

triage.headline_ja: 高性能エンテロウイルスワクチン、本日ベトナムで接種開始 予約殺到
triage.triage_reason: ワクチン接種開始に関する報道であり、疾病アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の異常事態を示す内容ではない。
triage.notes: 記事はEV71ワクチンの接種開始と需要の高さを報じるもので、感染症の発生・拡大を報告する内容ではないため、疾病発生地域としての対象国指定は行わない。

article.articleHeadline: Hadapi Musim Influenza A, Pentingnya Vaksinasi dan Menyiapkan Kebutuhan Kesehatan di Rumah
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Facing the Influenza A Season: The Importance of Vaccination and Preparing Healthcare Needs at Home.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A is a key seasonal respiratory infection in Indonesia, with subtypes H1N1 and H3N2 spreading via droplets in crowded settings. Symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, myalgias, and fatigue; complications can be severe in high-risk groups. Vaccination is a primary preventive measure, per WHO, reducing risk, symptom severity, and hospitalizations, though protection varies and is renewed annually due to viral change. In Indonesia, timing depends on epidemiology and vaccine availability; vaccines are ideally given before peak transmission, allowing about two weeks for antibody development. Target groups include children under five, adults 65+, pregnant women, those with chronic diseases, immunocompromised individuals, and healthcare workers. Alongside vaccination, practice hygiene, proper ventilation, masking when symptomatic, and keep home supplies (thermometer, masks, hand sanitizer, OTC symptom medicines). Antibiotics do not treat influenza; antivirals require prescription and are most beneficial early in illness. K24Klik supports online vaccination and medicine orders in Indonesia.

article.articleHeadline: Cornell researchers find mobile human gene in poxvirus | Fingerlakes1.com
article.articleSummary: Cornell researchers report two insertions of the human BC200 gene in the molluscum contagiosum virus (a skin-infecting poxvirus that can cause warts). The finding, published Sept. 24, 2026 in Science, documents a rare example of a human gene moving into a virus, estimated to have occurred about 100,000 years ago in skin cells. BC200 originated from a transposable element and dates to a common primate ancestor ~40 million years ago; in humans it is expressed mainly in neurons and may regulate neuronal mRNA translation, with low-level expression in sperm and eggs. The study does not show that BC200 alters viral behavior or enables cross-species transmission. Researchers led by Cedric Feschotte plan to test whether the virus uses the gene in infected cells. Funding sources include the National Natural Science Foundation of China, the University of Texas at Arlington, and Cornell.

article.articleSummary: Kisangani, in Tshopo Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, reports an Ebola virus disease situation. National MP Patrick Matata Makalamba called for vigilance and adherence to preventive measures in a 25 September 2026 statement. He urged the government and health-response teams to intensify public information campaigns, ensure near-care for patients, and supply health workers with protective equipment. Preventive actions highlighted include regular handwashing with soap and water, avoiding contact with Ebola patients or the bodies of deceased individuals, and promptly reporting suspected cases to the nearest health facility. He also advised avoiding bush meat and contact with dead animals, and stressed relying on official sources rather than rumors. The deputy urged neighborhood chiefs, religious leaders, teachers, media, and youth to raise awareness and combat stigma toward patients, survivors, and families affected by Ebola. Context notes the death of Dr Victor Kingombe amid the Kisangani Ebola situation.

In 59.39 sq km of targeted areas, 4,731 potential breeding sites were identified; 1,340 were sprayed by field teams, while drones operated for 40 hours 9 minutes. The drone survey covers 59.39 of the city’s 161.85 sq km examined so far, focusing on drains, water-logging, pits, and riverbeds where vectors breed. article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 85% of Indonesians Do Not Understand Pneumococcal Pneumonia, Here Are the Risks.
article.articleSummary: As of 25 September 2026, a YouGov survey in Indonesia shows low public understanding of pneumococcal pneumonia. Forty-one percent have never heard of pneumococcal pneumonia; 44% have heard the term but do not understand the disease; only 15% both know and understand. Among adults, 28% know that those aged 50 and over are at higher risk of severe pneumococcal pneumonia. Pneumococcal pneumonia is a lung infection caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae. Many respondents mistake it for the flu (20%), while 48% are neutral on the comparison. Symptoms such as shortness of breath or chest pain require medical evaluation; severe breathing difficulty or sudden confusion demand urgent care. Risk factors include older age and chronic diseases like diabetes, heart disease, and chronic lung disease. Pfizer Indonesia launched the Jakarta campaign 'Lindungi Napasmu Jaga Momen Berarti' to raise awareness among adults, especially caregivers of the elderly, with 55% reporting they regularly care for older family members.

Laboratory confirmation remains focused on sentinel facilities; no expansion of testing beyond these sites. article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A Breakthrough in Disease Prevention and Control: For the First Time, VNVC Brings the EV71 Vaccine Against Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease to Vietnam.
article.articleSummary: Vietnam becomes the first Southeast Asian country to deploy the EV71 vaccine for hand, foot and mouth disease, through VNVC and Substipharm Biologics. On 25 September 2026, nearly 300 VNVC centers nationwide began administering the vaccine. Phase III data from Vietnam, involving about 2,500 children, show 96.8% effectiveness against EV71 and no EV71 cases in the vaccinated group. The vaccine is indicated for children aged 2 months to under 6 years, with a 2–3 dose schedule depending on starting age. Taiwan’s CDC reported over 600,000 doses used from August 2023 to September 2026, with no severe HFMD (EV71) cases from 2024–2026 since vaccination began, whereas prior seasons saw many severe cases. Officials, including VNVC Medical Director Bạch Thị Chính, emphasize the vaccine as a crucial tool to reduce hospitalizations and complications. Public enthusiasm observed in Hanoi and across the country with thousands of registrations.

article.articleSummary: On Sept 25, 2026, GaoDuan Vaccine (6547) announced its Enterovirus 71 (EV71) vaccine has begun nationwide vaccination in Vietnam via VNVC, establishing about 300 vaccination centers. On day one, registrations reportedly exceeded 10,000 across Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Da Nang, Can Tho and other regions, with roughly 70% of enrollees under age 3, indicating strong family demand for EV71 protection. GaoDuan is the first—and currently the only—EV71 vaccine developed for Vietnam’s public vaccination system. Ahead of deployment, VNVC and Substipharm Biologics organized EV71 science symposia in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi on Sept 21–22, inviting Taiwan pediatric infectious disease and neonatology experts to discuss disease burden, clinical evidence, and real-world vaccination experience. Discussions addressed vaccine durability, the need for boosters in under-2s, and comparisons with other EV71 vaccines to support Vietnam’s immunization strategy.

article.articleHeadline: RDC : un jeune médecin succombe à Ebola à Kisangani
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: a young doctor succumbs to Ebola in Kisangani.
article.articleSummary: Dr. Victor Kingombe, a young internist in Kisangani, Democratic Republic of Congo, died of Ebola at a treatment center opened less than two weeks earlier. The outbreak, centered in Ituri, is spreading to neighboring provinces, with North Kivu reporting a 73% rise in infections over three weeks. The current epidemic is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, though vaccines targeting the Zaire ebolavirus (Ervebo) have shown partial protection, and August vaccination campaigns reached Kisangani health workers. Attacks on treatment and burial teams, community mistrust, and insecurity complicate response amid ongoing population movements. The WHO warned the outbreak could surpass the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic, which claimed over 11,000 lives. Local officials urged seriousness as authorities continue trials of treatments and post-exposure prophylaxis across the country.

article.articleHeadline: Why Is Fever Increasing In Chennai? Understanding Seasonal Infections
article.articleSummary: Respiratory viral infections, notably influenza, H1N1, and COVID-19, are rising in Chennai due to heavier Aug-Sep monsoon rainfall, with similar trends across India. Dengue cases are increasing as after-rains mosquito breeding surges. Concurrent increases in gastroenteritis and typhoid reflect broader non-viral bacterial infections. Fever alone is not diagnostic; most viral infections are short, while typhoid and similar bacterial infections may last beyond a week. A fever persisting five days or more, or signs such as shortness of breath, severe urinary pain, persistent diarrhea, jaundice, high-grade fever with chills, warrant medical evaluation. Preventive measures from the COVID era remain important: masks for vulnerable individuals, staying home when unwell, hand hygiene, eliminating standing water, safe water/food, and good ventilation in workplaces. Avoid self-medication and consult a physician for appropriate diagnosis and treatment, especially to distinguish viral from bacterial infections.

Andrey Demin commented that the increase in cases should not trigger an epidemic in the kingdom, citing high herd immunity and a virus that is more contagious but less deadly.
